purpose: Controls deliberately left without a HIPAA citation. Each was reviewed on 2026-10-06: its previous citation did not describe what the evaluator checks, and no Security Rule standard or implementation specification is a close enough match to cite instead. An empty citation is more accurate than a stretched one. NRG.FrameworkCoverage.Tests.ps1 accepts an empty HIPAA citation only for a control listed here, and fails if a listed control gains one (remove it from this list when a reviewed citation is added).

controls.PVW-2.3: Checks the Information Barriers mode. Its previous citation, 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(A), applies only to a health care clearinghouse within a larger organization, which the tool cannot establish; no other specification describes segmenting communication between internal groups.
controls.DEF-4.4: Checks that accounts are tagged as priority accounts in Defender for Office 365. Tagging is a prerequisite for differentiated protection and alerting, not itself a safeguard the Security Rule names; its previous citation, security reminders (164.308(a)(5)(ii)(A)), is workforce training.
controls.EXO-5.2: Checks that tagged priority accounts are protected by targeted user impersonation protection in the anti-phishing policy. Impersonation protection is not protection from malicious software (164.308(a)(5)(ii)(B)), and its previous citation, security reminders, is workforce training.
controls.TMS-1.5: Checks that Teams meeting recordings are stored in SharePoint/OneDrive under the organization's retention. Its remaining citation, 164.310(d)(2)(ii) media re-use, covers removing ePHI from electronic media before the media is reused, which the check does not examine (found by review of PR #121, 2026-10-07); no other specification describes where recordings are stored.
